gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Snapmaker sizes the Artisan enclosure's stock exhaust fan (36 CFM) for the 10W laser only, and sells a 95 CFM Boosted Exhaust Fan ($17.99) for its 20W/40W modules. Nor does any say that the $429 40W module fits every Snapmaker 2.0 model except the A150, which takes the 20W only.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us /topics/3d-printer-laser-combos/ (cited), desktop3dprinters.us /lists/3d-printers-with-laser-engraver/ (rank 1) and 3dengr.com (cited). Tom's Hardware (cited) blocked all fetches, so I could not compare against it. The desktop3dprinters pages already cover several limits: the H2S takes only the 10W module, the H2D/H2C take 10W or 40W, a standard H2 needs the Laser Upgrade Kit, the A250T/A350T take 10/20/40W, and the Artisan lists 20W and 1064 nm modules. 3dengr says you need a 'laser-ready' H2D. None of the three gives the Artisan enclosure's fan rating or the boosted fan for 20W/40W. None names the A150's 20W-only limit, the separate Power-Boosted Toolhead Cable the 40W module uses on Snapmaker 2.0, or that the Quick Swap Toolhead Plate does not fit the 200W CNC module.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. A buyer who chooses the Artisan as the 3-in-1 for the 40W laser should add the $17.99 Boosted Exhaust Fan, because Snapmaker rates the stock enclosure fan for 10W only. Snapmaker's US store also says the Artisan Enclosure cannot be bought online (you contact info@snapmaker.com), which makes an enclosure bundle like RobotShop's the practical way to get one. ChatGPT's 'budget' Snapmaker 2.0 A250T/A350T can move up to the 40W module ($429 at Snapmaker US). The 2.0 model where that fails is the smaller A150, which tops out at the 20W module. For the Bambu H2 series, the rival pages already state the 10W/40W limits.

findings.label: Artisan Enclosure purchase channel
findings.value: The maker says it is not sold online; you buy it by emailing info@snapmaker.com
findings.source_title: Snapmaker 40W Laser Module with Air Assist – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: Quoted: 'The Artisan Enclosure is not available for online purchase. Kindly contact our customer service team at info@snapmaker.com'.

findings.label: Enclosure exhaust fan rating vs laser power
findings.value: Stock enclosure fan is 36 CFM, which Snapmaker calls sufficient for the 10W module; the 95 CFM Boosted Exhaust Fan ($17.99) is pitched for 20W/40W use
findings.source_title: Boosted Exhaust Fan for Snapmaker Artisan – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: Quoted: 'particularly beneficial when using the 20W/40W Laser Module. (Note: The included Exhaust Fan in the package of Enclosure for Snapmaker Artisan has a maximum airflow of 36CFM, which is sufficient for the use of the 10W Laser Module.)' Snapmaker calls the boosted fan optional ('If you desire better fume extraction, you can upgrade it'). Compatibility: Enclosure for Snapmaker Artisan. Read via storecheck.

findings.label: 40W laser connection cable
findings.value: The 40W module connects to the controller through a Power-Boosted Toolhead Cable, sold as a spare part for $27.99; Snapmaker lists it for the Snapmaker 2.0 Series excluding the A150
findings.source_title: Power-Boosted Toolhead Cable For 40w Laser Module – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: Quoted: 'This cable is used to connect the 40W Laser Module and Controller. Compatibility • Snapmaker 2.0 Series (Excluding A150)'. I could not confirm from a maker page whether the 40W module's box includes this cable, so do not present it as an extra cost.

findings.label: 40W-specific spares exclusion

findings.source_title: Laser Safety Shield Kit For 40w Laser Module – Snapmaker US store
findings.note: Read via storecheck. It also lists the Artisan Series and Ray Series as compatible.
